name: perms
summary: All permutations of a vector's elements, one per row, in reverse lexicographic order of their positions.
doc: perms(1:3) starts with [3 2 1] and ends with [1 2 3]. The result has factorial(n) rows of n columns, in the class of v (numeric, logical or char). For a cell array, permute indices: C(perms(1:numel(C))).
differs: Its result is limited to 8 MiB: the permutations of 8 elements of a double or char vector, or 9 of an 8-bit integer or logical one; more are refused.
Cell and string arrays are refused; permute an index vector instead.
